system.name: BitTokens
system.one_liner: A single-token number encoding that represents any number via its IEEE 754 binary floating-point form, so small LMs can do arithmetic accurately with few tokens.

content.variant_note: a qualitative performance-versus-tokens plane on which three model types answer the same prompt in thought bubbles
content.argues: Reasoning LLMs get arithmetic right only with long token-hungry chains and basic LLMs are cheap but wrong; BitTokens are both accurate and cheap.
content.subject: One multiplication prompt answered by three model types placed on a performance-versus-tokens plane, with a long reasoning transcript.

lessons.what_to_learn: Place model types on a qualitative performance-versus-cost plane and let each answer the same prompt in a thought bubble with a tick or cross; show the expensive method's cost by drawing its real transcript at full length beside it.
lessons.suits: Motivation figures that must show a method is both accurate and cheap against a slow-but-right baseline and a fast-but-wrong baseline.

evidence: LLMs perform poorly on arithmetic tasks, requiring excessive reasoning tokens to achieve good performance.
reasoning chains can be very inefficient, sometimes requiring tens of thousands of tokens to solve a single calculation
Our BitTokens tokenization strategy allows language models to solve arithmetic tasks both effectively and efficiently.

summary: BitTokens encode any number as one token built from its IEEE 754 binary floating-point representation, so small language models can learn arithmetic algorithms without long reasoning chains or number splitting. Figure 1 is a motivation sketch. A prompt pill at the top asks 'What is 4314.97 × 4080000?'. Below it, a qualitative plane with gradient axes (arithmetic performance up in green, required tokens to the right in red) holds three model types drawn as network glyphs: LLMs with BitTokens at the top left, answering correctly in one short bubble; LLMs with Reasoning at the top right, also correct but followed by a long light-blue transcript of step-by-step checking; and Basic LLMs at the bottom, cheap but giving a wrong number marked with a red cross.
summary_zh: BitTokens 用 IEEE 754 浮点位表示把任意数字编码成单个 token。图 1 为定性示意：顶部给出乘法题，下方的“性能—所需 token”平面上，BitTokens 一句话答对，推理模型答对但附长篇推理，基础模型廉价却答错。
notes: Prior labels kept (concept-schematic, side-by-side-contrast). The plane has no tick values, so schematic-plot applies. The correct product is 17,605,077,600; the basic-LLM answer is off by a factor of about 1000. The three network glyphs and the brain are small bitmaps, the axis arrows are gradient bitmaps.
